feature: Validated staged append for split HDF5 datasets

gzip.checks: Exact full and spatially sliced fields, coordinates, topology, locations and weights; existing compressed chunk and geometry file unchanged.

zstd.checks: Exact full and spatially sliced fields, coordinates, topology, locations and weights; existing compressed chunk and geometry file unchanged.

gzip.checks: Exact coordinates, integer connectivity, cp and cf in all four frames, including both appended frames

zstd.checks: Exact coordinates, integer connectivity, cp and cf in all four frames, including both appended frames

behavior: Existing raw compressed chunks and geometry remain unchanged.
Append inherits uniform stored field filters and validates storage precision, zones, field schema and geometry.
Duplicate numeric timestamps and append+overwrite are rejected.
Staged incomplete snapshots and uncommitted frames are hidden from readers and descriptor regeneration.
Abandoned staging is discarded on a subsequent append; partial snapshot resume is not implemented.
Descriptor replacement failure after data commit retains the old descriptor; regeneration repairs it.
Relocated identical geometry can be supplied explicitly; reference updated on commit.
limits: No concurrent writers or SWMR/live reader refresh.
No filesystem/power-loss or HDF5 corruption durability guarantee.
Explicit append requires the split-geometry schema; legacy converter output is unsupported.
Real application check uses four surface snapshots in one zone, two fields, gzip and Zstd; external files are not unit fixtures.
No full volume append or Barnard append application test was run.
